userStories.title: Surface worktree and changed-file git failures
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Surface genuine git failures in worktree setup and smart change detection while retaining their existing expected fail-open cases.

**Motivation** — Failures that read as success hand callers a well-formed empty answer or silently continue after a real git failure.

**Approach** — Introduce `_worktreeManagerDeps = { gitWithTimeout }` in `src/worktree/manager.ts` and route **all seven** `gitWithTimeout` calls in that file through it. Give `WorktreeManager.remove` a distinct `WORKTREE_NOT_FOUND` code for the not-found stderr shapes it already enumerates, keeping `WORKTREE_ERROR` for genuine failures. Make `create()`'s Step-2 catch discriminate: silent for `WORKTREE_NOT_FOUND`, a structured `logger.warn("worktree", …)` for anything else. It still proceeds to `worktree add`. Add `gitWithTimeout` to the existing `_gitUtilDeps` in `src/verification/smart-runner.ts` and route both `getChangedNonTestFiles` and `getChangedTestFiles` through it. Log a `logger.warn("verification", …)` in both functions before every `return []` that is caused by a non-zero git exit or a thrown spawn, carrying the ref and the stderr or error message.

**Scope** — In: worktree git seam/error classification and smart-runner git warning paths. Out: TDD numstat behavior and cleanup polling (US-002); filesystem shell-outs (US-003).

**Interface** — `export const _worktreeManagerDeps = { gitWithTimeout };` is an `@internal` test seam. `WorktreeManager.remove` throws `NaxError(…, "WORKTREE_NOT_FOUND")` for the listed not-found shapes and `NaxError(…, "WORKTREE_ERROR")` otherwise. `gitWithTimeout` is added to the existing exported `_gitUtilDeps` object.
acceptanceCriteria: When `_worktreeManagerDeps.gitWithTimeout` resolves `{ exitCode: 1, stdout: "", stderr: "fatal: 'x' is not a working tree" }`, then `WorktreeManager.remove(projectRoot, "US-001")` rejects with a `NaxError` whose `code` is `"WORKTREE_NOT_FOUND"`.

When the worktree git seam resolves `{ exitCode: 1, stdout: "", stderr: "fatal: could not lock ref" }`, then `WorktreeManager.remove(projectRoot, "US-001")` rejects with a `NaxError` whose `code` is `"WORKTREE_ERROR"` and message contains `could not lock ref`.

When prune and add exit 0 and remove exits 1 with `fatal: could not lock ref`, then `WorktreeManager.create(projectRoot, "US-001")` resolves and `withWarnSpy` records a `logger.warn` with stage `"worktree"` whose data carries `"US-001"` and `could not lock ref`.

When prune and add exit 0 and remove exits 1 with `fatal: 'x' is not a working tree`, then `WorktreeManager.create(projectRoot, "US-001")` resolves and `withWarnSpy` records no `logger.warn` with stage `"worktree"`.

When `_gitUtilDeps.gitWithTimeout` resolves exit 128 with stderr `fatal: bad revision 'HEAD~1'`, then `getChangedNonTestFiles` returns an empty array and `withWarnSpy` records a `logger.warn` with stage `"verification"` whose data carries `bad revision`.

When `_gitUtilDeps.gitWithTimeout` resolves exit 128 with stderr `fatal: bad revision 'HEAD~1'`, then `getChangedTestFiles` returns an empty array and `withWarnSpy` records a `logger.warn` with stage `"verification"`.

When `_gitUtilDeps.gitWithTimeout` rejects with message `spawn EACCES`, then `getChangedNonTestFiles` returns an empty array and `withWarnSpy` records a `logger.warn` with stage `"verification"` whose data carries `spawn EACCES`.

When `_gitUtilDeps.gitWithTimeout` resolves exit 0 with `src/a.ts\nsrc/b.ts\n`, then `getChangedNonTestFiles` returns an array containing `src/a.ts` and `src/b.ts` and records no `logger.warn` with stage `"verification"`.

routing.reasoning: Two existing modules receive small, established dependency-seam and warning-path changes with independently mockable git results.

userStories.title: Make TDD git failures loud and cleanup grace waits bounded
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Honour `git diff --numstat` failures and replace the cleanup grace sleep with a bounded early-exit poll.

**Motivation** — A failed numstat currently becomes an empty map and a git hiccup is reported as a test-writer offence, while cleanup waits the full grace period even after the group dies.

**Approach** — `getAddedLinesPerFile` rejects with `NaxError(…, "GIT_ERROR")` when `git diff --numstat` exits non-zero, instead of discarding the exit code and returning an empty `Map`. `verifyTestWriterIsolation` in lite mode catches that rejection, logs `logger.warn("tdd-isolation", …)`, and completes with the strict-mode disposition — the check never rejects because numstat failed. Replace `cleanupProcessTree`'s single `sleep(gracePeriodMs)` with a bounded poll over `hasLiveGroupMembers(pgid)`, exported interval `CLEANUP_GRACE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`, capped at `ceil(gracePeriodMs / CLEANUP_GRACE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS)` iterations so it terminates under an injected instant `sleep`. The SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL contract is unchanged: `SIGKILL` is still sent, and only sent, when the group is still populated at the end of the grace window.

**Scope** — In: TDD isolation error policy and process-tree grace behavior. Out: worktree/change-detection warnings (US-001) and filesystem scans (US-003).

**Interface** — `export const CLEANUP_GRACE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` is a positive poll interval well under the 3000 ms default. `getAddedLinesPerFile(workdir, fromRef)` rejects with `NaxError(…, "GIT_ERROR")` carrying git stderr on non-zero numstat.
acceptanceCriteria: When `_isolationDeps.spawn` makes `git diff --numstat` exit 1 with stderr `fatal: bad revision 'HEAD'`, then `getAddedLinesPerFile(workdir, "HEAD")` rejects with `NaxError` code `"GIT_ERROR"` and a message containing `bad revision`.
When `_isolationDeps.spawn` makes `git diff --numstat` exit 0 with stdout `3\t0\tsrc/a.ts\n`, then `getAddedLinesPerFile(workdir, "HEAD")` returns a map with `src/a.ts` mapped to `3`.
When `--name-only` returns `src/a.ts` and `--numstat` exits 1, then `verifyTestWriterIsolation(workdir, "HEAD", [], [], "lite")` resolves and its violations contain `src/a.ts`.
When lite isolation encounters that numstat failure, then `withWarnSpy` records a `logger.warn` with stage `"tdd-isolation"`.

When strict isolation runs under the same git stub, then `verifyTestWriterIsolation(workdir, "HEAD", [], [], "strict")` resolves and records no `logger.warn` with stage `"tdd-isolation"`, because strict mode never requests numstat.
When imported from `tdd/cleanup`, then `CLEANUP_GRACE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` is a number greater than zero and strictly less than `3000`.

When the initial `ps` reports pgid `12345` and later probes report an empty group, then `cleanupProcessTree(12345, 3000)` sends exactly one `SIGTERM` and injected sleep arguments sum to no more than `CLEANUP_GRACE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`.

When every group-membership probe reports pgid `12345` populated, then `cleanupProcessTree(12345, 3000)` sends exactly `SIGTERM` then `SIGKILL` and calls injected sleep no more than `Math.ceil(3000 / CLEANUP_GRACE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS)` times.

routing.reasoning: The isolation and cleanup changes use established injected spawn and sleep seams with a bounded, deterministic polling algorithm.

userStories.title: Use native filesystem APIs for context and test scanning
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace init-context and test-directory shell-outs with native filesystem operations without changing scan contracts.

**Motivation** — PATH-resolved probes and ignored shell exit codes cost subprocesses and can silently turn a failed operation into an empty successful result.

**Approach** — `src/cli/init-context.ts`: replace the `mkdir -p` spawn with an in-process recursive create (`mkdir(path, { recursive: true })` from `node:fs/promises` is what the rest of `src/` uses), and surface a failure as a `NaxError` with code `"INIT_ERROR"` instead of ignoring the exit code. Replace the `find` spawn in `findFiles` with an in-process directory walk — `Bun.Glob` is the natural fit, but the choice is not normative. What is normative is the contract it must preserve: repo-relative paths, `node_modules` / `.git` / `dist` excluded, capped at `maxFiles`. `src/context/test-scanner.ts`: introduce `_testScannerDeps = { stat }` and replace both `Bun.spawn(["test", "-d", …])` probes with it. A path that exists but is not a directory must still be treated as `no test directory`, exactly as `test -d`'s non-zero exit does today.

**Scope** — In: native mkdir/walk and test-directory stat seam. Out: project scan fail-open disposition, which remains an empty file tree; TDD polling (US-002).

**Interface** — `export const _testScannerDeps = { stat };` is an `@internal` test seam. `initContext` reports mkdir failure as `NaxError(…, "INIT_ERROR")`.
acceptanceCriteria: When a temporary root contains `nested/deep/a.ts`, then `scanProject(root).fileTree` contains the exact repo-relative entry `nested/deep/a.ts` with no leading separator or root-path prefix.
When a regular file already exists at `.nax` in the temporary root, then `initContext(root)` rejects with `NaxError` code `"INIT_ERROR"`.
When `_testScannerDeps.stat` rejects for every path, then `scanTestFiles` for a temporary root containing `test/foo.test.ts` returns an empty array.

When `_testScannerDeps.stat` records paths and delegates to the real stat implementation, then `scanTestFiles` for a temporary root containing `test/foo.test.ts` returns that file and records the root's `test` subdirectory.
When `test` is a regular file rather than a directory, then `scanTestFiles` returns an empty array.

routing.reasoning: Two contained native filesystem substitutions with defined compatibility contracts and a standard seam.

userStories.title: Resolve interaction logger at call time and restore webhook globals
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make Telegram warnings see the initialized logger and make the webhook compatibility patch lifetime reversible.

**Motivation** — A plugin constructed before logger initialization loses all later warnings, while a process-wide Bun/fetch patch has no way back.

**Approach** — `src/interaction/plugins/telegram.ts`: drop the `private readonly logger = getSafeLogger()` field initializer and resolve `getSafeLogger()` at each of its eight call sites, mirroring `webhook.ts:161-166` and its written rationale. `src/interaction/plugins/webhook-serve-compat.ts`: `installServePortZeroCompat()` returns a restore function that reinstates the captured `Bun.serve` and `globalThis.fetch` and clears `servePortZeroCompatInstalled`. A re-entrant `installServePortZeroCompat()` returns a no-op restore, so the second caller cannot uninstall the first caller's patch. `src/interaction/plugins/webhook.ts`: `startServer()` stores the returned restore and `stopServer()` invokes it, so the patch lives exactly as long as the server does.

**Scope** — In: Telegram logger lookup and webhook compat installation/cleanup lifecycle. Out: unrelated interaction plugin behavior and global patch behavior beyond port-zero compatibility.

**Interface** — `installServePortZeroCompat(): () => void`; the restore reinstates captured `Bun.serve` and `globalThis.fetch` and clears the installation flag. A re-entrant invocation returns a no-op restore.
acceptanceCriteria: When `TelegramInteractionPlugin` is constructed after logger reset, then logger initialization followed by `init({ botToken: "t", chatId: "@channelname" })` records a `logger.warn` with stage `"interaction"` reporting the chat id is not numeric.
When the same construction and logger initialization order uses `init({ botToken: "t", chatId: "12345" })`, then no `logger.warn` with stage `"interaction"` is recorded.
When `installServePortZeroCompat()` is called, then it returns a function whose invocation restores `globalThis.fetch` to the exact pre-install function object.
When the restore returned by `installServePortZeroCompat()` is invoked, then `Bun.serve` is restored to the exact pre-install function object.
When `installServePortZeroCompat()` is called while already installed, then invoking its returned restore leaves `globalThis.fetch` equal to the patched function installed by the first call.

When a `WebhookInteractionPlugin` initialized with a loopback callback URL receives `receive("req-1", 1)` and is then destroyed, then `globalThis.fetch` equals the exact function object present before `receive`.

routing.reasoning: The reversible patch has process-global ownership and server lifecycle interactions across three modules, so isolated test and implementation sessions reduce regression risk.

modifiedFiles.reason: the test named "installing is idempotent and only patches globals once" calls `installServePortZeroCompat()` for its side effect and ignores the return value. No assertion in it is inverted by this story, so it is not a deadlock: it stays green exactly as written. What it is missing is the other half of the new contract. Extend that one test so it also asserts the restore returned by the *second* call is a no-op — invoking it must leave `Bun.serve` and `globalThis.fetch` still equal to the patched functions the first call installed. Keep both existing identity assertions unchanged; they remain correct and must continue to pass.

suggestedCriteria: When `installServePortZeroCompat()` is called twice, then the second call leaves `Bun.serve` and `globalThis.fetch` equal to the first patched values and its restore is a no-op.

userStories.title: Resolve idle-watchdog defaults from their source of truth
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Centralize idle-watchdog default resolution and preserve explicit ACP zero timeouts.

**Motivation** — Defaults that are not the default give omitted watchdog settings a 30-second timeout where the schema promises fifteen minutes.

**Approach** — Add `resolveIdleWatchdogSettings(config)` to `src/runtime/middleware/idle-watchdog.ts`, folding every absent field from `DEFAULT_AGENT_IDLE_WATCHDOG_CONFIG` and converting the seconds-valued fields to milliseconds. `attachAgentIdleWatchdog` reads its five settings from that resolver instead of the five inline `??` defaults, three of which contradict the SSOT: `30` against `900`, `0` against `1800`, and `5` against `10`. `src/agents/manager.ts:462` and `src/agents/retry/hop-retry-policy.ts:85` read `maxRetryAttempts` from the resolver instead of re-defaulting `?? 3` inline. `src/agents/acp/spawn-client.ts:92`: replace `timeoutSeconds || 1800` with `timeoutSeconds ?? DEFAULT_ACP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` so an explicit `0` is not silently promoted to 1800, and widen the field from `private readonly` to `readonly` so the resolved value is observable without spawning a session.

**Scope** — In: shared watchdog resolution, its three production consumers, and ACP timeout default. Out: ENH-45 permission behavior and unrelated pricing/default corrections.

**Interface** — `resolveIdleWatchdogSettings(config) => { idleTimeoutMs, toolCallOnlyTimeoutMs, graceMs, maxRetryAttempts, activityKinds }`; the parameter is structurally typed as an optional `agent.idleWatchdog` block, not `NaxConfig`, because `attachAgentIdleWatchdog` passes `NaxConfig` but `trySameAgentRetry` holds only the `AgentManagerConfig` selector slice. `export const DEFAULT_ACP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`; `SpawnAcpClient.timeoutSeconds` is `readonly`.
acceptanceCriteria: When `resolveIdleWatchdogSettings` is imported from `runtime/middleware/idle-watchdog` and receives enabled warn-then-cancel watchdog config with all timing fields absent, then it returns `idleTimeoutMs` of `900000`.
When `resolveIdleWatchdogSettings` receives that config, then it returns `toolCallOnlyTimeoutMs` of `1800000`.
When `resolveIdleWatchdogSettings` receives that config, then it returns `graceMs` of `10000`.
When `resolveIdleWatchdogSettings` receives that config, then it returns `maxRetryAttempts` of `3`.
When `resolveIdleWatchdogSettings` receives `cancelGraceSeconds: 0`, then it returns `graceMs` of `0` without replacing the explicit zero.
When `trySameAgentRetry` receives no `agent.idleWatchdog` block, a retriable `fail-stale` failure, and `staleRetryAttempts` of `2`, then it returns outcome `"stale-retry"`.

When `trySameAgentRetry` receives the same config and failure with `staleRetryAttempts` of `3`, then it returns `null` because the shared default cap is three and no other retry arm matches `fail-stale`.

When `SpawnAcpClient` is constructed with `timeoutSeconds` of `0`, then its `timeoutSeconds` is `0`; when constructed without the argument, then its `timeoutSeconds` equals `DEFAULT_ACP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`.

routing.reasoning: A structurally typed shared resolver changes defaults across runtime, manager, retry, and ACP consumers while preserving explicit zero values.

analysis:
This is a five-story remediation of existing Bun/TypeScript subsystems, with no dependency chain and no overlapping implementation files. Worktree creation/removal is centralized in src/worktree/manager.ts:12-340; create() currently swallows every Step-2 remove() failure at :144-151 and remove() maps listed not-found stderr shapes to WORKTREE_ERROR at :229-258. Its 13 callers include pipeline/worktree consumers and integration tests, so preserving create()'s clean-slate continuation is critical. src/verification/smart-runner.ts:41-43 already exposes _gitUtilDeps but only contains getGitRoot, providing the established seam for gitWithTimeout; its changed-file helpers must keep their existing fail-open arrays while logging. TDD isolation already has the injectable _isolationDeps seam at src/tdd/isolation.ts:25-26 and a bounded git runner; getAddedLinesPerFile() at :146-156 currently discards exitCode, while verifyTestWriterIsolation() at :229-268 directly awaits it in lite mode. The migration is local: make numstat failure explicit, catch only at the lite policy boundary, and retain strict mode’s no-numstat behavior. Cleanup uses _cleanupDeps at src/tdd/cleanup.ts:7-19 and cleanupProcessTree() at :102-138 does SIGTERM, unconditional sleep, then a group-member probe; replace only the wait mechanism while preserving group semantics and best-effort outer catch.

CLI context generation shells out in src/cli/init-context.ts:18-65: bunMkdirp ignores mkdir failure and findFiles shells out then strips the root prefix; scanProject() at :174-192 and initContext() are existing consumers covered by test/unit/cli/init-context.test.ts. The native walk must preserve relative paths, exclusions, 200-file cap, and the existing fail-open scan result. src/context/test-scanner.ts imports stat at :9, yet scanTestFiles() at :257-359 probes the directory with Bun.spawn([test, -d]); add the same exported mutable @internal seam convention as isolation without changing downstream glob/read behavior.

Interaction changes span Telegram, webhook, and compat code. TelegramInteractionPlugin caches getSafeLogger() in its class field (src/interaction/plugins/telegram.ts:54-613), whereas webhook call-time resolution is the sibling pattern. installServePortZeroCompat() at src/interaction/plugins/webhook-serve-compat.ts:94-140 globally patches Bun.serve/fetch behind a flag and currently returns void; startServer is its production caller, so webhook’s server lifecycle must own and invoke the new restore. Existing webhook compat and Telegram unit tests provide regression homes. Re-entrant restores must not unpatch an owner’s active global shim.

Idle-watchdog configuration is cross-module but remains a contained shared resolver. DEFAULT_AGENT_IDLE_WATCHDOG_CONFIG is defined in src/config/schemas-infra.ts:213-229. attachAgentIdleWatchdog() at src/runtime/middleware/idle-watchdog.ts:199-350 independently defaults 30/0/5 seconds and must use a structurally typed resolver because retry policy holds an AgentManagerConfig slice. trySameAgentRetry() at src/agents/retry/hop-retry-policy.ts:75-152 separately defaults stale retries to 3; src/agents/manager.ts is the third consumer noted in the spec. SpawnAcpClient at src/agents/acp/spawn-client.ts:44-297 assigns timeoutSeconds || 1800 and has a private field, so changing to ?? plus exported DEFAULT_ACP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is backward-compatible except that explicit zero now intentionally survives and the value becomes observable. Tests should extend existing focused suites and create only the story-named new test files. No config migration is required: omitted values resolve from the existing schema SSOT; explicit configured values, including zero, continue to win.
outOfScope:
ENH-45 — whether `resolvePermissions` should keep failing **open** to `approve-all` when
  `permissionProfile` is unset, and whether its sibling `default:` arm should keep failing closed
  to `approve-reads`, is a permission-contract decision reserved for a human ruling. Neither
  disposition changes in this sweep, and no logging is added to either arm.

SEC-12 — threading resolved permissions into `closePhysicalSession`, or exporting a named
  close-path constant from `permissions.ts`, is architecture rather than remediation and is
  deferred with ENH-45.

BUG-15 — the stale `MODEL_PRICING` rows are not corrected here; the correct rates are facts
  about the outside world that no test in this repository can establish.

TYPE-17, TYPE-38 and BUG-36 — type-annotation and cosmetic corrections with no observable
  runtime behaviour. None can be expressed as a runtime acceptance criterion.

BUG-37 — the uncaughtException/unhandledRejection hard exit deadline is not added; exercising it
  requires driving real process teardown from inside the suite that would host the test.

PERF-19 and PERF-31 — performance work whose only honest acceptance criterion is a timing
  threshold. Note that `cleanupProcessTree`'s poll is *not* in this class: it is asserted by
  counting injected `sleep` calls, never by wall-clock timing.

STYLE-42, STYLE-43 and STYLE-44 — the `QueueManager` deletion, the `routeTask`/`keywordRoute`
  consolidation, and the 16 grandfathered oversized files. Each needs a human decision about blast
  radius, and the file-size ratchet is a standing baseline rather than a discrete fix.

The disposition of an unavailable `git diff --numstat` in lite isolation mode is unchanged: the
  affected source files remain **hard** violations. This sweep makes that outcome loud, not
  different. Choosing a softer disposition needs data on how often numstat actually fails.

No import-cycle, `check:nax-error` or `check:file-sizes` baseline is lowered by this sweep; the
  existing baselines stand.

The project scan's fail-open when a directory cannot be listed is preserved, not pinned: it
  still yields an empty file tree rather than raising. Only the API doing the listing changes, and
  no criterion here asserts that disposition.
